added.title: Design Director Product Design Prototyping
added.description:
Job Description

Job Description :

Design Director, Product Design and Prototyping

The job in one line

You lead the design of products. You define what they should be, you build working prototypes of them yourself, and you shape how they go to market.

Why this role exists

Most agencies answer a product question with a deck. We want to answer it with something running on a phone.

We are a creative team inside a company that builds and runs technology for some of the largest companies in the world. That is an unusual place to sit. It means the products we imagine are products we are actually positioned to build. What we have been missing is the person in the middle: someone who can hold the product idea, the interface, and the market story at the same time, and who can make a real version of it in days instead of quarters.

That person did not exist five years ago at a price anyone could afford. Building a convincing prototype used to require an engineer. It does not anymore. AI tools have moved the hard part from writing the code to knowing what to build and having the taste to judge it when it appears. That is a creative job, and it sits on our team.

What you will do

Define the product. Decide what the thing is. Which features, in what order, for which customer, solving which problem. You will write the kind of clear product definition a client can act on and an engineering team can build from — user stories, feature prioritization and acceptance criteria for the MVP, a roadmap past it, the go-to-market plan, and the foundation for how success gets measured once it is live. You will do this on client work, on pitches, and on products we invent ourselves.

Prototype it. Not slides of a product. The product. You will build interactive, clickable, working prototypes using AI tools such as Claude Code, Claude Design, Cursor, v0, Figma Make, and whatever replaces them next year. Fast and rough on Monday, convincing enough to put in front of a client CEO by Friday. Your prototypes are how the rest of us find out whether the idea is any good.

Land it. Design the go-to-market alongside the product itself. How it launches, who it is for, what it promises, how it gets adopted, how it earns its second version. On this team, the product and the story it tells are the same piece of work.

Lead the work through. You will direct the designers on the products you define — setting the bar, running the critique, making the calls when the work needs to get better. The prototype is yours alone. Everything after it is a team, and you lead it.

What this looks like in practice

A retail client asks us to reimagine their app. In week one you and a strategist map where the current app fails its customer. By week two you have written a feature definition and built three working prototypes of the ideas that matter most, so the pitch team is arguing about a real interaction instead of a wireframe. By week three you have the launch narrative. When we win, you stay on it and lead the design of the thing you defined. Then you do it again for a transportation client's AI travel companion, again for a product we are building for the C-suite, and again for the next one.

How we will know it is working

The prototypes are the visible part. The measurable part is what they do to everything downstream. Engineering teams ramp onto new client work faster, because the product is defined and demonstrable before they arrive. Analytics, QA and user testing set up faster, for the same reason. New business gets a working prototype in front of a client sooner and more often. Proactive ideation goes up in volume, because ideas can be shown instead of described. And we lean less on off-the-shelf capability, because building the right thing stops being expensive.

Who this is for

We are looking for one person who can hold three things at once. People arrive at that from different directions, and we are open about which.

You may come from product.

You have been a product manager or product leader who was never satisfied handing off a requirements document. You have shipped real products people use. You have opinions about interfaces. Somewhere in the last two years you started building your own prototypes with AI tools instead of waiting for a sprint, and you have not stopped.

You may come from creative technology or design engineering.

You have been the person in the agency who makes the thing that wins the pitch. You can code, or you can direct AI tools to code, well enough that your prototypes feel real. What you want next is ownership of the product itself, not just the demo of it. You are applying to be the person who decides what gets made and makes the first version of it.

What We Will Ask You To Show Us

We do not need an advertising reel. Bring us products you defined and shipped, and be ready to explain what you decided and why, including the decisions you got wrong. Bring us prototypes you built with your own hands, and walk us through the tools and the process. If you have a launch you shaped, bring the thinking behind it: who it was for, what it promised, how it landed. Three or four things, told well, beats a portfolio site.

What you will need

Ten or more years of work, with real seniority in product, product design, or creative technology. Demonstrated ownership of products that shipped, not just features that were specified. Fluency with AI-assisted building. This is not a bonus line at the bottom of the posting. It is most of the job. You should already be using these tools daily and have views about which ones are worth anything.

Enough technical understanding to talk credibly with engineers, scope what is feasible, and know when a prototype is lying about how hard something will be. Design judgment. You do not have to be the person who makes it beautiful, and you will work alongside people who are. But you have to know beautiful from ordinary and be able to say why. The ability to stand in front of a client's leadership and hold the room.

What this role is not

It is not a software engineering role. You will not own production code, you will not be on call, and you do not report into engineering. It is not a visual design role. There is design craft in this job, but it is in service of the product, and you will have designers around you. It is not a support function for other people's ideas. This is a seat where the ideas start. On the panel: yes, and for a different question than the last three. The other postings had one audience. This one has two — the candidate, and whoever approves the title and band. The document is written entirely for the first. Nothing in it is phrased in the vocabulary a job-architecture reviewer uses to size a role, which is the thing you actually need it to survive. So I'd seat it for that: a compensation or job-architecture analyst on whether this reads as a Design Director-band role, an executive recruiter who places hybrid product-creative people on whether the market recognizes what you're describing, and someone who's held this shape of job on whether the description matches the reality. Plus the random seat. That panel answers a question worth answering. A panel on tone would mostly tell you the writing is fine.

NBCUniversal’s Ad Sales One Platform Ad Products team builds and operates the systems that power NBCUniversal’s $10B+ advertising business, including core ad serving, programmatic, and activation capabilities across CTV and digital.

Within AP&S, the Programmatic Demand team is responsible for product strategy and development of demand-side capabilities across NBCU’s programmatic ecosystem.

We are seeking a Senior Product Manager, Programmatic Demand

This role focuses on developing scalable products, systems, and workflows that improve programmatic demand performance across NBCU’s ad tech stack.

You will identify inefficiencies in auction dynamics, platform behavior, and partner integrations—and translate those insights into durable product solutions rather than one-off optimizations.

A key focus area will be live event monetization, where concurrency, DSP behavior, and system constraints introduce complex demand-side challenges that require structured, product-led solutions.

Platform Configuration & Deal Strategy

Improve how platform settings (e.g., in FreeWheel and partner DSPs) translate into predictable demand performance

Who We Are:

ACAMS is the global leader in certification, training, and intelligence for anti-financial crime (AFC) professionals. ACAMS sets the standard for how organizations prevent, detect, and respond to money laundering, fraud and sanctions evasion. Trusted by 70% of the world's leading banks, as well as governmental and law enforcement agencies, and FinTechs, the organization has 120,000+ members across 200+ countries and territories. Its 65+ chapters and annual conferences connect AFC professionals across every major financial center. Learn more at acams.org.

Position Summary And Areas Of Responsibility

This newly created senior leadership role is responsible for defining and executing ACAMS' commercial product strategy across our training portfolio and digital ecosystem. The role will drive portfolio growth, market expansion, customer value, and commercial performance by developing compelling value propositions, optimizing pricing and packaging strategies, and ensuring ACAMS' offerings remain aligned with evolving industry needs. Working closely with the Chief Product Officer and cross-functional leaders, the successful candidate will translate market insights and strategic priorities into growth initiatives, investment decisions, and scalable solutions that strengthen ACAMS' market leadership and deliver sustainable business results.

Accountable for driving growth and the performance of ACAMS' training portfolio and digital ecosystem, including certification and certificate programs, enterprise solutions, pricing and packaging, this position will oversee portfolio strategy, commercial performance through the lifecycle of products. Success will be measured through business growth, revenue performance, customer adoption, market impact, and the ability to capitalize on emerging opportunities across global markets including creating new products from existing content.

A key responsibility will be shaping portfolio priorities through customer insights, market intelligence, competitive analysis, and commercial evaluation. The position will work closely with Product, Technology, Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success teams to ensure offerings are differentiated, commercially successful, and deliver measurable value for customers and the business.

In partnership with Sales, Marketing, and Customer Success, the successful candidate will lead go-to-market strategies that drive acquisition, retention, expansion, and cross-sell opportunities. This includes defining segment-specific value propositions and growth strategies across enterprise, and individual professionals.

The position will lead a team of senior product managers, providing strategic direction, coaching, and portfolio oversight, while fostering a culture of customer focus, accountability, innovation, and commercial excellence.

As a senior leader, the successful candidate will act as a trusted advisor to senior sales leaders and executive stakeholders representing ACAMS with key customers, partners, and industry practitioners. Foster a culture of commercial excellence, customer focus, and continuous improvement while championing product management best practices and data-driven decision-making. Define target segments, assess market attractiveness, and evaluate ACAMS positioning to inform strategic decisions. We're hiring a Product Manager (Technical) to be our product’s right hand as Osmo scales its Software and AI organization. This is a hands-on product role, not a program management role — you'll own scoping, requirements, and delivery negotiation directly, working independently from day one.

Your first mandate: Osmo's internal workflows are largely manual today, and information doesn't always flow through our systems the way it should. You'll identify the 3-5 tools that would drive 80% of the impact, embed with the relevant teams to master the problem, and come out with clear requirements that get built. From there, expect to move across workstreams as priorities shift, applying the same structural skills to a new domain. You'll work closely with engineering throughout, and you'll need to hold your own there: when an estimate doesn't add up, you push back with specifics, ask for the breakdown, and know how to simplify a requirement to get something shipped faster. This role takes real tenacity to drive scope and delivery under ambiguity, and real kindness in how you ask a stretched engineering team for more.

What You'll Do

Scope With Rigor — Independently scope projects end to end: understand the business value and customer need, then write clear, complete requirements that inform what engineering builds.
Negotiate Scope and Estimates — When an engineering estimate doesn't match reality, push back with tenacity: ask for the breakdown, identify what's actually driving the cost, and simplify or revise the requirement to get to a faster, leaner build.
Find the 80% — Scope Osmo's highest-value internal tooling opportunities: identify the 3-5 tools that would drive the majority of workflow impact, then sequence and prioritize the build.
Embed and Master — Rapidly insert yourself into a workstream, understand it deeply, and come out with the requirements and plan to fix what's broken.
Partner Directly With Engineering — Work hand-in-hand with the CTO’s team to get scoped work built and delivered against committed dates.
Operate Without a Script — Take high-level direction into an ambiguous space and bring back clarity, milestones, and a plan — with the curiosity to figure out what's actually needed rather than waiting to be told.
Bring Structure Without Bureaucracy — Sequence and manage ambiguous initiatives without adding process for its own sake.
Pivot With the Business — Move fluidly across workstreams as Osmo's priorities shift, applying the same core PM skill set to new problems.

Direct Engineering Collaboration, Non-Negotiable — You have worked hands-on with engineering teams in a prior role. You know how to sit across from an engineering lead, question an estimate, and land on a scope that actually reflects the work.

About VGS

VGS is the world's leader in payment tokenization, trusted by the most innovative AI and Fortune 500 companies, merchants, banks, and fintechs to power modern payments and agentic commerce.
We tokenize over 9 billion tokens and process more than 10 billion monthly interactions, touching a third of all e-commerce. That scale isn't incidental. It's why leading companies embed our universal token vault and credential management platform directly into their stack, taming the complexity of payment data so they can move faster.
We’re helping businesses unlock new possibilities in an industry that never stops moving. And that takes exceptional people.

About the Role

As Product Manager for Network Services, you will own our relationships with card networks and payment gateways. You will define new network capabilities, lead their integration into the VGS Credential Management Platform (CMP), and deliver them to customers through tokenization, account updater, wallets, Local Payment Methods and card-on-file services. This role requires end-to-end execution—from initial partner conversations to scaling capabilities across our entire customer base.

What You'll Do

Product Strategy & Network Relations:
Define the technical roadmap for network integrations, partnering directly with major card networks and payment gateways to scope upcoming capabilities.
Normalize Network Differences:
Abstract network-specific quirks (e.g., real-time vs. batch updates, differing subscription models, unique event types) into a unified, predictable API experience for VGS customers regardless of the underlying network.
API Design & Feature Spe cs:
Define API interfaces, functional requirements, and webhook event models built for long-term durability, ensuring schema updates won't break existing customer integrations.
Cross-Functional Execution:
Partner directly with Engineering, Security, UX, and Legal to validate designs, translate complex network updates into execution plans, and guide features from early partner discussions through beta to general availability.
Launch & Customer Enablement:
Own customer onboarding, integration support, and implementation guides, partnering with engineering to deliver clear API documentation and developer tools.
Data & Performance:
Define and track platform KPIs: network integration cycle time, feature adoption rate across customers, API/webhook reliability (uptime, latency, error rate), and network SLA compliance, and write custom SQL queries to analyze usage patterns and inform product decisions.

What You Bring

Experience:
7+ years in product management or digital product development with a strong focus on launching B2B platforms, developer APIs, or payments infrastructure.
Technical Grounding:
Ability to read network specifications, debate trade-offs with engineers, and design APIs/webhooks that scale smoothly.
Data Proficiency: Hands-on with data and comfortable writing SQL queries to pull usage metrics, track adoption, and defend product decisions.
Operational Leadership:
A detail-oriented problem solver who thrives in fast-paced environments, leading execution even when scope or priorities are still evolving.

Nice to Have:

Experience with tokenization, payment processing, cryptology, or security products
BA/BS degree
A knack for out-of-the-box thinking that thrives in a fast-paced startup environment
Experience with authentication services, EMV, 3DS specifications.
Background building cloud-native applications or high-throughput global platforms.

$175,000 - $225,000 a year

What We Look For In Every Teammate

We're looking for passionate professionals who take pride in their craft and want to help grow a team tackling some of the most critical problems in payments. People who thrive here are curious by nature, unafraid of hard problems, and motivated by the chance to build something that matters at scale.

If you're driven to make a meaningful impact, work at the leading edge of payment technology, and grow your career alongside a team that values ownership, collaboration, and continuous learning, you'll feel right at home at VGS.

At VGS, we embrace a remote-first philosophy because we believe flexibility leads to great work and a healthy work-life balance. That said, if you live within 30 miles of one of our office locations, you'll be on a hybrid schedule with some in-person time, because we know there's real value in coming together.

We're not about being in the office every day. We are about connection, collaboration, and the energy that comes from a great brainstorm, a team lunch, or celebrating a big win in person.
